chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Kahili, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A house was shared among a group of people who divided it, and each took a portion, built upon it, and left a courtyard between them for their passage. Then a man came and bought the share of one of them. Is that permissible for him? He said: 'Yes, but he must close his door and open a door to the road, or descend from above the house and close his door. And if the owner of the road wishes to sell it to him, they have more right to it; otherwise, it is his road, and he comes and sits at that door.'

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِهِ: More entitled to it (right of pre-emption)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a new co-owner regarding shared courtyards and roads in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the mechanics of *shuf'ah* (pre-emption) regarding shared residential structures, specifically addressing the rights of co-owners when a new party acquires a share. It establishes that while the new owner may utilize common areas, they must secure access for others, yet the original co-owners retain the primary right to purchase the specific shared portion if they choose, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving communal harmony and preventing unilateral disruption of shared utilities.
